# Design Patterns

> The 22 Gang of Four patterns and more than 60 system design patterns. A free guide from DesignGurus.io, in plain Markdown, with no account required.

Each page is short and ends with links to full course lessons and free articles. Each description below is the opening sentence of that page.

## Code patterns

- [Chain of Responsibility](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/behavioral/chain-of-responsibility.md): Pass a request along a line of handlers until one of them deals with it.
- [Command](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/behavioral/command.md): Turn a request into an object, so it can be queued, logged, retried, or undone.
- [Iterator](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/behavioral/iterator.md): Walk a collection without exposing how it stores its items.
- [Mediator](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/behavioral/mediator.md): Route object-to-object communication through one coordinator, so components stop knowing each other.
- [Memento](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/behavioral/memento.md): Capture an object's state so it can be restored later, without exposing what is inside it.
- [Observer](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/behavioral/observer.md): Notify many dependents when one object changes, without the source knowing who they are.
- [State](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/behavioral/state.md): Let an object change its behavior when its internal state changes, instead of checking a status field everywhere.
- [Strategy](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/behavioral/strategy.md): Swap an algorithm at runtime behind one interface, instead of branching on a type inside the caller.
- [Template Method](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/behavioral/template-method.md): Fix the steps of an algorithm in a base class, and let subclasses fill in the steps that differ.
- [Visitor](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/behavioral/visitor.md): Add a new operation to a class hierarchy without editing any of its classes.
- [Abstract Factory](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/creational/abstract-factory.md): Create families of related objects that must match, without naming their concrete classes.
- [Builder](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/creational/builder.md): Assemble a complex object step by step, so callers never face a constructor with twelve arguments.
- [Factory Method](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/creational/factory-method.md): Let a subclass decide which concrete type to create, without the base class knowing the type exists.
- [Prototype](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/creational/prototype.md): Create a new object by copying a configured one, instead of building it from scratch.
- [Singleton](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/creational/singleton.md): One instance of a class, with one place that owns its lifecycle.
- [Adapter](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/structural/adapter.md): Make an incompatible interface fit the one your code already expects.
- [Bridge](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/structural/bridge.md): Split one class into two hierarchies that vary independently, before they multiply into a class explosion.
- [Composite](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/structural/composite.md): Treat a single object and a tree of objects through the same interface.
- [Decorator](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/structural/decorator.md): Add behavior to one object at runtime, without touching its class and without a subclass per combination.
- [Facade](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/structural/facade.md): Put one simple entry point in front of a subsystem that is more complicated than most callers need.
- [Flyweight](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/structural/flyweight.md): Share the part of the state that repeats, so millions of objects fit in memory.
- [Proxy](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/code-patterns/structural/proxy.md): Stand in for another object, with the same interface, to control access, cost, or timing.

## System patterns

- [Feature Store](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/ai-systems/feature-store.md): Compute a feature once, and serve the identical value to training and to production.
- [GPU Auto-Scaling](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/ai-systems/gpu-autoscaling.md): Scaling the most expensive machine you rent, when cold start is measured in minutes.
- [LLM Gateway](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/ai-systems/llm-gateway.md): One control point for keys, quotas, routing, fallbacks, and cost per team.
- [Model Serving](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/ai-systems/model-serving.md): Put a model behind an API, with batching, versions, and a way back.
- [RAG Pipeline](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/ai-systems/rag-pipeline.md): Retrieval, ranking, and generation as one system, with failure modes at every stage.
- [Semantic Caching](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/ai-systems/semantic-caching.md): Reuse an answer for a question that is similar, not identical.
- [Vector Database Sharding](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/ai-systems/vector-database-sharding.md): Splitting an index whose accuracy depends on seeing enough of it.
- [API Versioning](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/api-edge/api-versioning.md): Change a contract without breaking clients you do not control.
- [Backend for Frontend](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/api-edge/backend-for-frontend.md): One API per client type, instead of one API that fits none of them.
- [Cursor-Based Pagination](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/api-edge/cursor-pagination.md): Page through changing data without skipping or repeating rows, which offset pagination cannot do.
- [Service Mesh](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/api-edge/service-mesh.md): Sidecars with a control plane.
- [Sidecar](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/api-edge/sidecar.md): Move cross-cutting concerns out of the application process and into a container beside it.
- [Cache-Aside](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/caching/cache-aside.md): The application checks the cache, and on a miss it loads from the database and puts the result back.
- [Cache Stampede Prevention](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/caching/cache-stampede-prevention.md): Stop a thousand requests from rebuilding the same expired key at the same moment.
- [Read-Through](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/caching/read-through.md): The cache loads from the database itself, so callers never see the data source.
- [Write-Behind](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/caching/write-behind.md): Acknowledge the write immediately, persist it a moment later, and accept that the moment is a window where data can be lost.
- [Write-Through](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/caching/write-through.md): Write to the cache and the database together, before acknowledging.
- [Event-Driven Architecture](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/communication/event-driven-architecture.md): Services coordinate through facts that already happened, instead of commands telling each other what to do.
- [Publish-Subscribe](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/communication/publish-subscribe.md): One event, many independent consumers, and a publisher that knows none of them.
- [Request-Response](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/communication/request-response.md): The caller sends a message and waits for the answer.
- [Webhooks](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/communication/webhooks.md): You call them when something happens, so they stop polling you.
- [Saga](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/consistency/saga.md): A long transaction split into local steps, each with a compensating action, and no global lock anywhere.
- [Change Data Capture](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/data-intensive/change-data-capture.md): Turn database writes into a stream, without asking the application to publish anything.
- [Exactly-Once Semantics](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/data-intensive/exactly-once-semantics.md): What it actually means, why the naive version is impossible, and how real systems get the effect anyway.
- [Partitioned Consumption](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/data-intensive/partitioned-consumption.md): Parallel consumers, with ordering preserved inside each key.
- [Blue-Green Deployment](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/operations/blue-green-deployment.md): Two complete environments and one switch.
- [Canary Deployment](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/operations/canary-deployment.md): Expose a small share of real traffic to the new version, and let the metrics decide.
- [Distributed Tracing](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/operations/distributed-tracing.md): Follow one request across every service it touched, when the logs are in twelve places.
- [Feature Flags](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/operations/feature-flags.md): Separate deploying code from releasing behavior, and accept the debt that follows.
- [Bulkhead](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/reliability/bulkhead.md): Partition resources so one sick dependency cannot drown the whole service.
- [Dead Letter Queue](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/reliability/dead-letter-queue.md): Somewhere to put the message that will never succeed, so the queue keeps moving.
- [Graceful Degradation](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/reliability/graceful-degradation.md): Serve something useful when the ideal answer is not available.
- [Retry with Exponential Backoff](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/reliability/retry-exponential-backoff.md): Try again, waiting longer each time, with randomness, and with a budget.
- [Timeout](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/reliability/timeout.md): A bound on how long you are willing to be stuck.
- [Auto-Scaling](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/scaling/auto-scaling.md): Match capacity to load automatically.
- [Connection Pooling](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/scaling/connection-pooling.md): Reuse connections instead of opening one per request, and stop the database running out of them.
- [Horizontal Scaling](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/scaling/horizontal-scaling.md): More machines, which forces you to deal with state.
- [Vertical Scaling](https://github.com/design-gurus/design-patterns/blob/main/system-patterns/scaling/vertical-scaling.md): Get a bigger machine.
